vectors.name: both-output-with-payloads
vectors.description: Both parties learn the result size and hold the association table, and each records its own input row count (recordsExposed); each sends and receives one payload column under a named data-sharing agreement. Exercises the full governance block -- a legal-agreement reference, purpose, and expiration, payload columns with data-dictionary descriptions sent and received, the psi algorithm, and the matching basis (the ssn linkage field, recorded as name + type) -- alongside the commitments, plus the run binder a signed exchange carries so its placement in the record is pinned across implementations. Fixed salts and binding nonce make the build deterministic so any implementation must reproduce these bytes.

vectors.name: no-data-payloads
vectors.description: Both parties hold the association table but neither sends payload columns and no legal agreement is configured. The governance block records the psi algorithm and the matching basis (the ssn linkage field) with empty sent/received payload lists and no legalAgreement -- the no-payload case represented explicitly rather than by ambiguous omission. Each commits an empty (no-data) payload as the canonical empty-arrays value; confirms the sent and received no-data cases serialize identically across implementations.

vectors.name: single-output-sender
vectors.description: A single-output sender: the local party's terms set expectsOutput false and the partner's set it true, so this party receives no output. It holds no association table (no associationTable commitment) and the result size is omitted (recorded only when both parties' terms have them both receive output); its own input row count is still recorded as recordsExposed, the per-direction figure that does not depend on entitlement. It sent its payload (one column, with a data-dictionary description) and received an empty one, so governance records a populated payloadSent and an empty payloadReceived. This is the sender's side of the same exchange as single-output-receiver below, so both reproduce the same termsHash, and this sent payload equals the receiver's received payload. Pins the canonical serialization of the single-output helper's disclosure entry: recordsExposed present, both the association-table commitment and resultSize absent.

vectors.name: single-output-receiver
vectors.description: A single-output receiver: the local party's terms set expectsOutput true and the partner's set it false. It receives output, so it holds the association table (associationTable commitment present), but the result size is still omitted because only one party receives output; recordsExposed still records its own input row count, as on every record. It sent an empty payload and received the partner's (one column, with a data-dictionary description), so governance records an empty payloadSent and a populated payloadReceived. This is the receiver's side of the same exchange as single-output-sender above (same agreed terms, hence the same termsHash; the received payload equals that vector's sent payload). Pins the only real combination no other vector covers: an association-table commitment present while resultSize is absent.

vectors.name: count-only-psi-c
vectors.description: A count-only psi-c exchange: both parties learn only the intersection size, so the result size is recorded (and each records its own recordsExposed count) but no association table is held or committed and no payload is exchanged. Exercises the psi-c algorithm (only a count was disclosed, not matched identifiers), a legal-agreement reference and purpose, empty sent/received payload lists, and a multi-field matching basis recorded as name + type and sorted by name. The terms also declare an unused linkage field (email_address) that no linkage key references; it is excluded from the matching basis, which therefore covers only the fields the keys actually matched on (dob, last, ssn4).

vectors.name: count-only-unicode-purpose
vectors.description: psi-c with a non-ASCII legal-agreement purpose (accented Latin, em dash, Cyrillic); pins that a purpose carrying non-ASCII flows through the record and termsHash byte-identically across the Node and browser builds.

vectors.name: both-output-with-retention-disposition
vectors.description: The both-output-with-payloads exchange, with this party's optional self-facing retention/disposition pointer set. The pointer is copied verbatim into this party's record and changes nothing else: the termsHash, the commitments, the binding nonce, and the opening are byte-identical to both-output-with-payloads, because the pointer is sourced from this party's local config (not the agreed linkage terms), is never swapped with the partner, and is not folded into the agreed-terms hash. Pins that retentionDisposition flows through to the record unmodified and that a record carrying it reproduces byte-identically across the Node and browser builds.

vectors.name: cited-rule-set-contradicted
vectors.description: The agreed terms cite both built-in rule sets over rules that are not those sets -- one field with no constraints and a key the set does not declare -- so governance carries the citation verbatim beside the writing party's own verdict on it, `contradicted` on each half. Verbatim is the point: the refuted claim stays in the record rather than being dropped, so the artifact states what was claimed as well as what this build found. Otherwise identical to no-data-payloads, so the pair pins both sides of the citation: present here, absent there, and absent by omission rather than by a null. The citation is part of the agreed terms, so it is folded into termsHash: this vector's hash differs from no-data-payloads' for that reason alone. The verdict is not -- it is written locally, after the hash, and never exchanged.

vectors.name: cited-rule-set-consistent
vectors.description: The mirror of cited-rule-set-contradicted: the same built-in citation over rules genuinely drawn from those sets -- the most precise built-in key and exactly the built-in fields it references -- so each half's verdict is `consistent`. A narrowed emission still counts as drawn from the set, which is what lets a run over an input file that cannot supply every key keep its citation. The pair pins that the verdict is computed from the declared rules rather than fixed by the presence of a citation.

vectors.name: cited-rule-set-unchecked
vectors.description: The third verdict: the agreed terms cite a rule set this build does not ship, so neither half resolves to anything to compare against and each verdict is `unchecked`. The declared rules are byte-identical to cited-rule-set-consistent's -- the built-in fields and the most precise built-in key -- which is what pins that a half is resolved by the cited NAME and content version rather than by the rules beside it: the same declarations reach `consistent` under a citation naming the shipped set and `unchecked` under one this build cannot resolve. The citation is recorded verbatim either way, so a reader can tell a name that was checked and matched from one nothing was compared against.

vectors.name: unnamed-local-party
vectors.description: The local party supplied no identity and the partner supplied one. `linkage_terms.identity` is optional, so the record omits `localIdentity` entirely rather than writing an empty string or a stand-in label, and keeps `partnerIdentity` beside it; pins that the absent and present halves serialize the same way across implementations, and that the terms hash is taken over terms carrying no identity key at all.

vectors.name: receipt-swap-terminated-with-binder
vectors.description: The same both-output exchange as the first vector, recorded after the run terminated past its payload exchange rather than completing. Pins the terminated outcome's placement and literal spelling across implementations, and pins the presence rule that goes with it: the binder is carried because the run derived one, not because this party holds a receipt, so a terminated record still pairs against a receipt the partner completed. Everything else is unchanged from that vector -- same commitments, same governance block, same exposed-record count and result size -- which is the format's statement that a terminated record attests the disclosure in full.

vectors.name: many-to-one-local-deduplicates
vectors.description: This party declared deduplicate and its partner did not, so its seat resolves to many-to-one: several of its records link to one of the partner's. Pins the governance block's resolved matching (localDeduplicate true, partnerDeduplicate false, cardinality many-to-one) and the commitment over an association table whose partner half repeats a row index once per link while its local half stays strictly ascending. The committed payloads hold one row per matched record rather than one per pair -- three sent rows for the three distinct local records, two received rows for the two distinct partner records those three pairs link to -- so an implementation committing a payload row per pair does not reproduce these commitments. The recorded result size is the pair count. The mirror seat of the same run is one-to-many-partner-deduplicates, whose termsHash is this one's.

vectors.name: one-to-many-partner-deduplicates
vectors.description: The partner seat of the run many-to-one-local-deduplicates records, with the two terms documents swapped: this party declared no deduplicate and its partner declared it, so the same run resolves to one-to-many here. Pins the mirrored label (localDeduplicate false, partnerDeduplicate true, cardinality one-to-many), which is the value an implementation reading the wrong side of the pair gets wrong, and the commitment over the mirrored association table -- the same pairs, ordered by this party's own row index, with the local half non-decreasing and the partner half strictly ascending. The payload directions swap with the seat and cover byte-identical data to the mirror vector's, while the two seats commit under different salts. The agreed-terms hash matches the mirror vector's, since the hash orders the two documents canonically rather than by which party is local.

vectors.name: many-to-many-both-deduplicate
vectors.description: Both parties declared deduplicate, so both seats resolve to many-to-many and each keeps its within-dataset duplicate values. Pins the resolved matching (both values true, cardinality many-to-many) and the commitment over an association table whose two halves both repeat: a two-by-two cluster of one matched value contributes four pairs and a fifth pair stands alone, so the recorded result size (5) is above either party's matched-record count (3). The committed payloads again hold one row per matched record, three on each side. The linkage strategy is cascade, the one that pairs the both-sided cardinality.
